_readme: Canonical intent publication registry (adopted 2026-11-14, owner-directed). Every published page maps to a canonical intent; a page may originate in any qualified language. This file records the intents whose hreflang cluster cannot be named by an English member: any cluster with no English page must have a record here, and any other cluster may. A cluster with an English member and no record has the implicit id legacy:<english path>. Membership is NOT stored here: it is the hreflang mesh, read by scripts/lib/intent-clusters.js. `pages` pins the record to its cluster (the origin page at least); the mesh supplies every other language. The id never changes when a language is added or the primary page moves. Model and field reference: docs/architecture/language-neutral-intents.md. Validated by `npm run check:canonical-intents` (CI-gated). A record is a normal intent registration, not an exception: no English page, planned or otherwise, is implied or required.

policy.xDefaultFallbackOrderReason: x-default serves visitors whose language no member matches. When a record declares no xDefault, the first member in a listed language is used; English is listed because it is the broadest fallback for an unmatched visitor and the site root's language. It is never the origin page by default, and a cluster with no listed-language member gets no x-default.

scopes.cross-language: The user need could meaningfully exist in more than one language. It does not mean any other language should be built; demand decides that.
scopes.locale-specific: The need's meaning or function cannot be the same intent in another language, with evidence (a script, orthography or register that exists only in one language). Missing demand data, zero volume or an unfamiliar translation is never evidence for this scope.
scopes.pending-review: The semantic question is open; the record states it in openQuestions. The page stays valid while it is open.

intents.scopeBasis: The page converts Japanese kana into ギャル文字 lookalike glyphs. The transform is defined on Japanese script and the register exists only in Japanese, so no other language can have the same page. Playful registers in other languages (leetspeak, alay, 火星文) are different transforms and would be their own intents.
